key_insight: Fine-tuned transformer language models can detect social isolation and social support cues in unstructured clinical notes, with FLAN-T5-Large performing best.
clinical_relevance: This approach could help EHR systems surface hidden social risk factors for more context-aware patient stratification and care planning.
method: Annotated clinical note spans with social context cues were used for fine-tuning.
Models compared included FLAN-T5-Large, BERT, RoBERTa, and Gemma-2-2B.
Performance was assessed using Accuracy, Precision, Recall, and Macro-F1 with structured prompting to reduce overgeneralization.
evidence_signal: FLAN-T5-Large achieved the highest Macro-F1 at 0.92±0.04, outperforming Gemma-2-2B (0.89±0.10), RoBERTa (0.80±0.21), and BERT (0.77±0.17).
watch_item: Real-world use may be limited by note variability, ambiguous context, and the need for careful validation before deployment in clinical workflows.
paper_title: Fine-Tuned Large Language Models for Detecting Social Isolation from Unstructured Clinical Notes
